machine: 6 cores, 32427 MiB available of 48092 MiB, 29 GiB/s on this model's matmul

decisions.label: Overlap I/O
decisions.brief: Off: the experts are computed on the device, beside its cache.
decisions.reason: overlap hides the CPU's expert compute behind the streamer's reads, and with the device expert cache armed the experts are computed on CUDA0, so there is nothing on the CPU for it to hide

decisions.label: Device expert cache
decisions.brief: A 4.1 GiB cache of the most used experts on CUDA0, in place of whole layers' experts.
decisions.reason: the experts used most live on the processor that computes them fastest, as the RAM cache holds what flash would read: CUDA0 computes this model's experts at 221 GiB/s against the host's 20, both measured on this model's own expert block; a cache of 4168 MiB (4050 the capacity fitter gave 6 of 48 layers' experts, 118 it left free under one more whole layer) serves 13% of a token's routed bytes (the fraction of the expert set it holds); a miss is uploaded from the host

decisions.label: Batch width
decisions.brief: A prompt runs in one pass: that takes only 932 MiB.
decisions.reason: a graph as wide as the context reserves 932 MiB of compute buffers, inside 10% of the 32427 MiB this process may hold: a prompt is computed in one pass

decisions.label: Layer placement
decisions.brief: 49 layers on a device; 48 of 48 layers keep their experts on the CPU.
decisions.reason: the capacity fitter found a placement that is projected to fit; 48 of 48 MoE layers keep their experts on the host, host-resident 932 MiB, on devices 10743 MiB, context 16384 (fitter's host breakdown: model 55626, context 0, compute 932 MiB; file 63336, experts 32400)

decisions.label: Context
decisions.brief: 16384 tokens of context, as given: not weighed against the cache.
decisions.reason: the value this run was given, not a choice: the capacity fitter only picks a context when it is handed a zero and this planner always pins it, so nothing has weighed this number against what the memory it reserves would buy as expert cache

decisions.label: Streaming mode
decisions.brief: Experts stream from storage: the model needs 33.5 GiB, 25.3 GiB is usable.
decisions.reason: on the host 34282 MiB (dense 1882) against 25941 MiB usable, which is the 32427 MiB this process may hold (as reported available, unmeasured) less a 6485 MiB margin (the process is killed)

decisions.label: Further offload
decisions.brief: Nothing beyond the layer placement moves to a device.
decisions.reason: the fitter has already placed what fits on the devices - see the placement line above - and placing weights across devices is a capacity problem it solves exactly; this planner owns the tier below it and does not second-guess it

decisions.label: Where experts live
decisions.brief: Experts compute on the CPU: no device can reach streamed memory.
decisions.reason: this device could compute them on paper - it offers a host buffer and runs the model's own layout - and it still cannot. The streamer rebinds every expert onto memory it reserved itself, which no device was given access to; and a host buffer type would not survive the load anyway, since a mapped model has one substituted for the CPU's. Whether this device can wrap memory a caller already owns - the one opening left - is unprobed. What it advertises is a blanket promise, and a backend whose support is conditional declines to make one while implementing the call anyway, so the absence of a yes decides nothing here

decisions.label: Dense weights
decisions.brief: Dense weights are copied into RAM, so they are never re-read from storage.
decisions.reason: no reclaim-exempt store here, so anonymous buffers are what keeps the dense set off a flash refault (a reclaim then means: the process is killed)

decisions.label: Prefill device
decisions.brief: Prompts are not given a device of their own: the experts are computed on the layers' device.
decisions.reason: a device expert cache is set, which keeps the layers on their device and computes the experts there; a prefill device is not combined with it

decisions.label: Tables left mapped
decisions.brief: The embedding tables (27.1 GiB) stay mapped: the graph gathers rows from them.
decisions.reason: the allocation priced the embedding group as mmap (left mapped: the graph gathers rows from it, so a token reads a few KiB of it however large the table is, and residency would buy bytes nothing reads), and the anon policy would otherwise copy its 27726 MiB into memory the ledger did not charge

decisions.label: Pin the cache
decisions.brief: The cache is not locked: not even one token's experts could be.
decisions.reason: not even one token cycle of the cache can be locked in place here after what is ahead of it, so the cache is ordinary memory and no lock is asked for

decisions.label: Memory use
decisions.brief: This run holds 22.2 GiB of the 25.3 GiB it may use.
decisions.reason: held 22731 of 25941 MiB holdable, of which locked 0 MiB of 0 MiB lockable: context and compute 932, context checkpoints 950, expert cache 20849

decisions.label: Storage speed
decisions.brief: Experts load at 2.0 GiB/s, in 450 KiB reads, 4 at a time.
decisions.reason: this model's expert slice is 450 KiB and at that request size this storage gives 2042 MiB/s over 4 lanes: the expert lane is priced there, not at the storage's peak

decisions.label: Cache floor
decisions.brief: The smallest cache that helps is 632 MiB, under the engine's usual 1.5 GiB minimum.
decisions.reason: the engine's fixed cache guard (1500 MiB) is above this model's token cycle (632 MiB), so a budget between the two returns hits and needs force-cache to be accepted; the floor enforced here is the model's

decisions.label: Device placement
decisions.brief: A device would be faster for some weights; this build cannot use it yet.
decisions.reason: a device won at least one group, but this build computes on the host: the placement is reported, not applied

decisions.label: Expert streaming
decisions.brief: Experts stream from storage; everything else stays in memory.
decisions.reason: the experts do not fit but the dense set does

decisions.label: Expert cache
decisions.brief: 20.4 GiB: what the cache earns most with, after the dense weights.
decisions.reason: what the cache is worth out of 25941 MiB usable, ranked against the resident groups by seconds saved per byte of RAM, with what none of them wanted added: 24058 MiB committed in total, of which 20849 MiB is cache, over a floor of 632 MiB

decisions.label: Checkpoint budget
decisions.brief: Context checkpoints may take 950 MiB; that is kept out of the cache.
decisions.reason: 8 checkpoints ("Context checkpoints") of 118 MiB each, the part of the context that does not grow with its length (measured at two lengths), charged before the cache is sized: a chat run fills them as it goes, and memory the cache had already taken would have to come out of something else

decisions.label: Read lanes
decisions.brief: 4 parallel reads: the fastest rate this storage gave.
decisions.reason: the highest measured rate for this model's 450 KiB expert slice on this storage

decisions.label: Direct I/O
decisions.brief: Reads bypass the page cache: checked correct on this storage.
decisions.reason: uncached reads return correct bytes on this path

decisions.label: Unmap the file after load
decisions.brief: The model's file mapping stays: this run still reads from it.
decisions.reason: this run keeps a live pointer into the mapping (a tied head, a draft block, a dense policy that stays mapped, or a table left mapped), so the mapping cannot be released whatever the storage does

decisions.label: Output quality
decisions.brief: Nothing that changes the output is turned on.
decisions.reason: no quality budget was given, and a policy that changes the output must never arm itself

decisions.label: Compute threads
decisions.brief: 6 threads: the fastest count measured on this model's format.
decisions.reason: swept over the thread counts this machine has, on a matmul in this model's own quantized format, which is the material that matters: a sweep in F32 can pick a count the quantized kernels are much slower at

decisions.label: Thread counts to measure
decisions.brief: The first answer measures 3 threads against 6.
decisions.reason: the thread count changes no output and which one decodes fastest is this machine's answer, not a rule's: once the cache has settled the first real request alternates decode windows between 6 and 3 (where a slower class of core starts, every core, or half of them where all are alike), and switches only to a count 10% faster in the median of its rounds; the next load starts from the verdict
